RCS of a sphere remains constant in all directions regardless of aspect angle.
Cylinder RCS is maximum at 180 degrees aspect angle and minimum at 90 and 270 degrees.
Ellipsoid RCS peaks at 90 and 270 degrees and is minimum at 180 degrees.
Triangular flat plate RCS is maximum at 0 and 180 degrees and minimum at 90 degrees.
Truncated cone RCS has maximum at 0 degrees and minimum near 80 degrees aspect angle.
Complex objects are modeled by vectorially adding RCS of constituent shapes.
Swerling models I and II correspond to Chi-square distributions with 2 degrees of freedom, modeling fluctuating RCS.
Swerling models III and IV correspond to Chi-square distributions with 4 degrees of freedom, modeling RCS with one large and one small scattering surface.
